report.summary: The patch at lib/assessment-label-citations.ts lines 105–117 follows the stated finite rule for implicit labels, which avoids a false whole-source absence claim or a cross-form combination when the implicit control's form owner cannot be positively resolved. However, the negative branch still treats a positive-declared implicit label with an empty text as a required label that a form has to group. That can cause a false 'no_complete_group' (definite absence) for a bare <label><input></label> whose input is implicitly bound to the form. The positive and citation paths correctly keep this case as 'declared'. The schema-derived completeness guidance (assessment-prompt-guidance.ts:6–10, wired at delivery-assessment.ts:184) remains generation advice, and the strict decoder still rejects a reply that omits a top-level key once (delivery-assessment.ts:250, validated by the test at tests/assessment-prompt-guidance.test.ts:101–110). The patch tests also still run the supplied cases through the single decoder. No other correctness defect was found inside the supplied packet.

findings.title: Implicit label with no text is still added to a form group, so a negative check can wrongly say the labels are absent
findings.evidence: When a label contains exactly one labelable control and that control has no form attribute, line 107 `if (nested.length === 1 && explicit === undefined) continue;` keeps `label.form` set to the label's ancestor form. Line 157 then includes it, because the condition `if (!labels.includes(label.text) || context === "form" && !label.form) continue;` checks only that text appears in the required labels. Line 160 `groups.get(owner)!.add(label.text)` stores the empty text "", and line 162 does not require the group to contain every required label as a non-empty fact. A bare `<label><input></label>` is an implicit label with empty text, but it still counts as producing text "" in form F. This is the same class of false whole-source absence finding that the patch was meant to eliminate for nested implicit labels. The positive branch and `labelsIn` citations avoid this through `label.parts.length` / `.filter(p => normalized(p.value))`, but the finite negative scan has no equivalent guard.
findings.reproduction: Not executed. Trace: the directive is context form, labels are ["Name", "E-mail"], the model reply has status changes_suggested, and the only HTML is '<!doctype html><html><body><form><label>Name</label><label><input></label></form><label>E-mail</label></body></html>'. Then: 'Name' → form F; the bare '<label><input></label>' → nested.length 1 and explicit undefined, so line 107 continues and line 157 adds text "" to F; the external '<label>E-mail</label>' (no control) is unowned, so it is skipped. groups = {F: {"Name", ""}} and F does not contain 'E-mail', so the function returns `{kind: "no_complete_group", context: "form", ...}` rather than an unknown. A marker-like empty label such as `<label><input type="checkbox"></label>` produces the same result.
findings.suggestion: In the negative scan, skip labels with no non-whitespace parts (for example, add `label.parts.length === 0` to the continue condition at line 157, or add no implicit placeholder labels there). That makes an empty implicit label leave ownership unresolved instead of adding a fact. Add a test case with a bare implicit label to the existing variants.

limitations: The review is read-only and only covers the six supplied files. It does not include lib/assessment-completion.ts, assessment-citation-selection.ts, assessment-response.ts, assessment-citation-catalog.ts, or the fixtures named in the test files, so their exact schemas and decoder messages were not checked directly.
No files were executed and no tests, typecheck, or build were run. Both the finding and the checks of the existing behaviour are reasoning traces over the supplied line-numbered source.

Coverage is limited to the finite-source-fact path in catalog_slots mode with status supported or changes_suggested and without saved business steps. The legacy_quotes and catalog_ids replay paths and the supported-status citation path were not re-derived in full.

Parse5's exact tree-shaping behaviour (for example, where a label or input ends up once a stray sub-form element is present) was not verified by running it. The finding relies on ordinary parse5 handling of a simple form, label and input.

The negative path's existing behaviour tied to form-owned explicit labels, foreign HTML detection, and unresolved-owner handling was checked only at the level of the supplied code. It was not checked against unseen corpora.
The follow-up corpus cases are known to the requester. They cannot be judged as new independent evidence until they are frozen and approved.
